declaredDeviations.description: The dossier's provisional command used Codex run-isolated. This protocol instead invokes the same safe_handler/store boundary directly from a deterministic adapter.
declaredDeviations.rationale: The LLM and host scheduler are outside the transaction-isolation question and would add an uncontrolled source of operation ordering, retries and missing ledger events. Host integration remains an explicit non-claim.

declaredDeviations.description: The dossier names a matched PostgreSQL reference cell; this protocol runs the complete four-level PostgreSQL ladder in both repetitions.
declaredDeviations.rationale: Using the same operation counts, concurrency levels and reversed repetition order avoids selecting one favorable PostgreSQL level after observing SQLite.

declaredDeviations.description: Temporary C1/C2 experiments run during runner/adapter development are development pilots only. They used a write recovery probe, an eager task backlog, the wrong queue boundary and no peak-connection observation; they are excluded from the release matrix and did not select any registered parameter.
declaredDeviations.rationale: Documented here, at freeze, so the pre-freeze tooling history is traceable without being mistaken for scored evidence; RESEARCH-PROCESS.md requires pilot observations that inform the final protocol to be written before any scored cell.

declaredDeviations.description: After the C1/C2 pilots above were corrected, two development smokes ran unscored outside any sealed release: the pinned baseline at concurrency 2, operations-per-type 1, produced the expected blocked oracle; the pinned candidate at concurrency 5, operations-per-type 100, produced a proven oracle with 3W+1 = 301 measured terminal operations, five dispatcher requests in flight and one request observed at the source admission queue.
declaredDeviations.rationale: These smokes validated the corrected runner/oracle machinery before registering the exact ladder levels and repetitions below; their temporary trees are excluded from publication and neither result selects a registered parameter after the fact.

declaredDeviations.description: A real PostgreSQL 17.9 producer-to-oracle smoke at concurrency 1, operations-per-type 1 ran during tooling development against the pinned candidate and returned a proven oracle verdict.
declaredDeviations.rationale: Established that the workload/oracle chain reconciles against a live PostgreSQL 17 service before registering the PostgreSQL provisioner and the full ladder; it is unscored and excluded from the release matrix, and did not select any registered PostgreSQL parameter.

nonClaims: The study does not establish a safe production concurrency above five requests or generalize throughput beyond this synthetic mutation fixture.
The study does not claim that cancelling an asyncio waiter cancels its native worker, and it never relabels a cancelled or transport-lost operation as rejected.
The study does not prove handler-wide atomicity after a store method has already committed; a larger unit-of-work contract is separate work.
The study does not measure embedding, predictive gating, wiki synchronization, MCP serialization, LLM quality, Claude/Codex host parity or complete-stack maturity.

The PostgreSQL reference uses an owner-private, credential-free local Unix-socket service. It does not evaluate authentication, TLS or networked PostgreSQL security, and databases are logically dedicated rather than isolated from other code running as the same operating-system user.
The scored full matrix is POSIX-only on the registered Linux or macOS host and its results are host-specific. Cross-platform validator conformance does not establish Windows workload support.

No external network access is required or intentionally performed, but external egress is neither blocked by an operating-system sandbox nor measured. The pinned source, adapter and runtime execute as trusted code under the same operating-system identity; this study is not a hostile-code isolation or data-loss-prevention evaluation.

The release binds the source locks, interpreter bytes, Python version, package/version inventory and reported native-library versions. It does not claim a byte-identical container, complete software bill of materials, or content hash for every installed package file.
Performance and saturation observations are descriptive; they are not correctness thresholds or winner scores.
